system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
## Buyer review — Project Kestrel

| Issue | Seller’s position | Buyer should want | Recommendation and one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001: General liability cap** | General Warranty Claims capped at **20% of price (AUD 4.8m)**. | At least **50% of price (AUD 12m)** for general warranties, with fundamental/title, tax, specific indemnities, covenants and fraud outside that cap. | **Reject and counter at 50%.** A 20% cap is inadequate for a private-company acquisition where several material risks remain unresolved. |
| **SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket** | AUD 25,000 de minimis; AUD 250,000 deductible basket, with only excess recoverable. | Lower thresholds—e.g. **AUD 10,000 de minimis and AUD 100,000 tipping basket**, with related claims aggregated and the full amount recoverable once crossed. | **Counter.** The proposed thresholds could exclude multiple meaningful claims and leave Buyer bearing the first AUD 250,000 of Seller warranty breaches. |
| **SPA-N-003: General claims time limit** | General claims must be notified within **18 months** after Completion. | At least **24–36 months**, with timely notification preserving a claim until finally resolved. | **Counter at 24 months minimum, preferably 36 months.** Eighteen months may expire before a second audit cycle exposes historical issues. |
| **SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title warranties receive the same 20% cap, thresholds and 18-month limit as general warranties. | Separate fundamental regime: **100% of purchase price cap**, no thresholds, and at least six years—or no contractual expiry for title. | **Reject.** Buyer must have full recourse if Seller lacked capacity or did not validly transfer 100% of the shares. |
| **SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance terms apply to all claims; no express fraud carve-out is offered. | Express disapplication of all caps, thresholds, time bars, knowledge, disclosure, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance protections for fraud, fraudulent concealment and deliberate or wilful misconduct. | **Insist on an express carve-out.** Seller must not benefit from contractual limitations in respect of dishonest conduct or concealment. |
| **SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope** | Blanket disclosure of the entire data room, accounts, registers and public records, without admitting materiality or legal consequence. | Only matters **fairly disclosed in sufficient detail** in the Disclosure Letter against identified warranties; no general disclosure of the data room or public records, and an updated disclosure package at signing/Completion. | **Reject general disclosure.** Depositing documents or referring to searchable records does not fairly identify the nature and likely consequences of an exception. |
| **SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for anything Buyer or its advisers knew or could discover from the data room or public records. | Preferably no knowledge bar; failing that, only **actual knowledge of named senior Buyer individuals**, excluding constructive knowledge, adviser knowledge and matters merely discoverable, with no application to indemnities, title, tax or fraud. | **Reject as drafted.** It improperly converts due diligence into a broad waiver and shifts the risk of incomplete Seller disclosure to Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent** | Seller uses reasonable endeavours; condition is satisfied by delivery of written consent, despite no evidence that clause 11.3 conditions have been met. | A true condition precedent requiring **final, unconditional and effective written consent**, satisfaction or waiver of all associated conditions, no adverse amendment, and Buyer approval of its form. | **Do not complete without satisfactory consent.** Bluefen represents approximately 30% of FY26 revenue, making conditional or ineffective consent unacceptable. |
| **SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility** | Approximately AUD 3.2m remains outstanding; security release will be supplied after Completion. | Repayment directly from Completion funds under an agreed payout letter, with **simultaneous irrevocable discharge and release of all security and guarantees** as a Completion deliverable. | **Reject post-Completion release.** A debt-free/cash-free acquisition cannot leave Buyer or the Company exposed to Seller-era debt or security after Completion. |
| **SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses** | AUD 420,000 Completion bonuses are Seller’s matter but are omitted from funds flow; on-costs are unspecified. | Seller to fund the bonuses and all payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs, with amounts treated as **Seller transaction expenses/debt-like items** and expressly shown in funds flow. | **Require a price deduction or direct Seller funding.** The bonuses are triggered by the sale and must not reduce the Company’s post-Completion cash. |
| **SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity** | Existing indemnity is limited to the specific unpaid SOW3 amount of AUD 180,000. | Pre-Completion payment, receipt and confirmatory IP assignment, plus a separate indemnity covering all losses from non-payment, defective ownership, transfer restrictions and related infringement or remediation. | **Broaden and place outside general limitations.** The risk is loss or impairment of ownership of Project Materials, not merely the unpaid invoice amount. |
| **SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident** | Characterised as preliminary and not expected to be material; access, scope and notification requirements remain unknown. | Prompt forensic investigation, preservation and disclosure of evidence, required notifications/remediation before Completion where practicable, and a specific indemnity for all pre-Completion incident losses, claims, response costs and penalties. | **Do not rely on the materiality assertion.** The incident potentially involves 1,240 records and its regulatory and remediation consequences have not been established. |
| **SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals** | Three AUD 110,000 renewals—AUD 330,000 aggregate—are said to be ordinary-course costs. | Full contracts and renewal dates, confirmation of termination rights and accrual/payment status, Buyer consent to any pre-Completion renewal, and proper treatment in working capital or as debt-like items where appropriate. | **Reserve position pending verification.** Calling the renewals ordinary course does not establish that the commitments are avoidable, correctly accrued or reflected in price. |
| **SPA-N-014: Category separation** | Seller proposes that limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all claims unless expressly excluded. | Clearly separate regimes for general warranties, fundamental/title, tax, specific indemnities, covenants and fraud, with distinct caps and periods and no cross-category erosion of caps. | **Reject an omnibus limitation regime.** Known and fundamental risks should not consume—or be constrained by—the limited general warranty recovery pool. |
| **SPA-N-015: Title verification** | Seller relies on the Company share register at DD-012 as evidence that it owns 100% of the shares. | Unqualified title warranties plus original certificates, ASIC and corporate records, Seller authority documents, confirmation of no options or third-party interests, and releases of all share encumbrances. | **Treat the register as evidence, not conclusive proof.** A company-maintained register alone does not establish clean legal and beneficial title free of encumbrances. |
| **SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms** | Seller treats tax and IP warranties as settled under the general 20%/18-month regime. | A tax deed covering all pre-Completion tax, with a statutory-period-plus buffer and up to 100% cap; enhanced IP ownership/infringement warranties and appropriate longer/higher protection, including the Ironquay indemnity. | **Keep both regimes open and reject general treatment.** Tax liabilities can emerge years later, while core IP ownership is central to the value of an analytics business. |

### Buyer priority points

The principal **no-completion/no-concession items** should be:

1. Effective Bluefen consent;
2. Riverlark repayment and simultaneous security releases;
3. Seller-funded bonuses and on-costs;
4. Confirmed Ironquay payment and IP ownership;
5. Specific protection for the export/privacy incident;
6. Full title protection; and
7. Express separation of fundamental, tax, indemnity and fraud claims from the general limitation regime.
=== END ADVICE ===
